title: topless.pro beach candidates
description: One file per region under data/<country-code>/<region>/beaches.json. This schema gives editors autocomplete and typo checks; the policy rules (evidence, publishing bar, slug uniqueness) are enforced by scripts/validate-beach-data.mjs.

countryCode.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, upper case; must match the country folder.

slug.description: Permanent: it is the URL and the database key. Renaming a slug creates a new beach and unpublishes the old one.

municipality.description: The municipality the local authority uses (Δήμος, commune, county); optional. Shown in the location line and the page title when present.

dressCode.description: What happens here. clothing-optional = nude and clothed use mix across the whole beach; nudity-permitted = nude bathing in a recognisable part only.

recognition.description: How firm the practice is: official (law, signage, designation), tolerated (established local practice), community-reported (unconfirmed), disputed (sources conflict).

confidence.description: Confidence in the dressCode, not in the beach's identity. high requires a sourceUrl.

summary.description: 1–3 sentences for visitors; required to publish. Appended to the search-result description after the name, place and classification and cut at 160 characters, so put the key fact in the first sentence.

sourceUrl.description: Evidence for the dress-code claim, not for the beach's existence. Map pins and link shorteners are rejected by the validator. Required to publish.

lastVerifiedAt.description: The day the source was last checked (YYYY-MM-DD, not in the future). Required to publish.
